newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON DENY REPORTS OF MOVE TO DUBLIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON DENY REPORTS OF MOVE TO DUBLIN.

text.p: The owner of English premier league Wimbledon on Thursday denied newspaper reports the club was on the verge of a move to Dublin despite year-long rumours to the contrary.

Sam Hammam, whose team currently shares the Selhurst Park ground in London with first division Crystal Palace, said the reports were misleading and a move to Ireland would only be considered as a last resort.
"We will only use that situation if we know that we can never go back to Wimbledon in a logical manner that is feasible and practical," Hammam told BBC Radio.
"Even if that fails, we will see if we can stay at Selhurst Park for ever and a day, which will need a detailed agreement with Crystal Palace."
"Anyone who gives credence to such stories is only embarrassing themselves. People are getting carried away by the story which is germinating in Ireland," he said.
Hammam admitted he had held talks with a consortium of Irish businessmen including Paul McGuinness, the manager of rock group U2, about a move to the Irish capital.
But he said: "There is a difference between meeting a girl and getting married."
Soccer's European governing body UEFA has said it totally opposes the move and would not sanction it.
"Wimbledon are an English club with a home in England and UEFA is not in favour of them moving to a foreign country," UEFA spokesman Salvatore Cuccu said.
"It goes against the spirit of football, of crossing national boundaries, and we are not in favour of it."
The move is also opposed in principle by the Football Association of Ireland, although the English FA say they have no policy on it.
